summary.text: On September 2, 2026, Lutnick described AI as an opportunity to broaden access to intelligence and improve productivity and societal prosperity. In April 2026, he advocated deploying American AI systems internationally, linking that effort to economic security, national security, and ties with partners. In June 2025, he criticized regulatory limits on innovators and said CAISI would promote commercial AI innovation while maintaining national-security standards.

stance_review.reason: Two statements establish enthusiastic general views of AI's societal benefits. The remaining excerpts address narrower applications, infrastructure, standards, trade, competition, or announcements rather than AI's overall effects. Supplied context resolves s6 as data-center advocacy and s27 as praise for NIST research; neither establishes a general AI stance. The findings do not imply that the bounded corpus captures all of Lutnick's views.
